html:
The Lenca are an Indigenous people of southwestern Honduras and eastern El Salvador, living in the highlands around Intibucá, Lempira and La Paz. With several hundred thousand people they are the largest Indigenous group in Honduras, though their Lencan languages have nearly all died out and most speak Spanish.

Before the conquest the Lenca lived in many small chiefdoms on the southern edge of Mesoamerica, trading with the Maya and other neighbours. In 1537 the Lenca leader Lempira rallied thousands of warriors against the Spanish and held out at the mountain fortress of Cerquín until he was killed, by tradition during a parley. Honduras named its currency, the lempira, after him. In 2016 the Lenca activist Berta Cáceres, who led opposition to a dam on the sacred Gualcarque River, was murdered. Their neighbours include the Pech, the Tolupan and the Cacaopera.
